What's new · Version 0.4.44

Heather keeps learning.

The latest release sharpens the guardian — she checks on herself through the day, speaks up in her own voice if something breaks she can't heal, and the screens that matter are clearer than ever.

Heather checks on herself

Through the day, Heather runs her own self-checks. If something breaks that she can't heal herself, she speaks up in her own voice and tells you — she never goes quiet and leaves you unguarded.

Clearer bypass labels

The bypass screen now shows its labels properly — including Spark Driver — so the few apps that refuse any VPN are easy to spot and set. Everything else stays behind the Moat, untouched.

Heather updates her own knowledge

Once a day, over Wi-Fi, Heather fetches the latest threat list herself — fresh trackers and malicious domains join her watch without waiting for an app release. She keeps learning, and there's still no cloud and no account: she takes in a list, and sends nothing about you.

Quiet apps stay connected

Games and other safe apps no longer lose their connection while they sit quiet — in menus, between rounds, in the background. The Moat only blocks threats; a safe app passes through untouched, exactly as it should.

Feel the moat

Every app on your phone is phoning home. VØID-SCRY hangs up.

Trackers and malicious domains try to connect quietly, in the background, all day. Raise the Moat and those connections die at the wall — before a single byte of you leaves.

    How it works

    Three layers. One silent guardian.

    No dashboard to learn, no feed to scroll, no chatbot to talk to. VØID-SCRY is built to disappear — and to be there the moment something reaches for your data.

    01

    The Moat

    A VPN-style protection layer sits between your apps and the internet. Every outgoing connection is checked against versioned threat intelligence — trackers, malicious domains, the quiet leeches — and the bad ones are turned away at the wall. Your apps work as normal; the surveillance doesn't.

    02

    The Watch — Heather

    Heather is an AI who lives entirely on the phone — no cloud, no account, no conversation. She watches over the Moat and judges what it catches. Her brain is resident only while there's judging to do, then it rests, so a guardian this smart still runs light on an ordinary phone.

    03

    The Proof

    Every week the phone writes its own report — what was blocked, what was watched, that protection held — generated on the device, from the device's own numbers. Not a promise from a company. Proof from your phone.

    Meet Heather

    She doesn't chat. She guards.

    Heather works under five standing mandates. They're not marketing — they're the rules she was built to, and they outrank every feature.

    Protect

    Your data and personal information are guarded first — before convenience, before everything.

    Watch

    She keeps watch over the phone's connections — including foreseeable threats, not just known ones.

    Regenerate

    Knocked down, she heals herself — restarts, restores, and stands guard again without being asked.

    Build ahead

    She fetches the latest threat list over Wi-Fi once a day, so her watchlist sharpens daily — the guard you have keeps getting smarter.

    Close the gap

    Protection extends to the whole household — every family phone carries its own full guardian.

    The No-Harm Principle

    VØID-SCRY is defense only. Everybody's personal information is protected — not just the owner's — and the guardian does no harm to others or their property. That principle outranks feature ambition, and it is binding on everything built on top of her.

    The proof

    Proven, not promised.

    This isn't a render of a product that might exist someday. VØID-SCRY is installed, running, and standing guard on a real phone right now — an ordinary one.

    Running today
    Live on Android — 35 people running it on their own phones — and proven on-device on a Galaxy A17, a basic phone with 4 GB of RAM. If it runs there, it runs anywhere.
    Blocked so far
    17,000+ trackers and malicious domains stopped on the live device — and the count climbs every day the phone is simply used as normal.
    Fail-closed option
    Proven on-device: if protection drops, it says so loudly — never silently. You are never left thinking you're guarded when you're not.
    Weekly proof reports
    Generated on the phone, from the phone's own numbers. The product audits itself, out loud, every week.

    Sealed storage

    Threat intelligence

    Self-healing

    Household protection

    One person's privacy shouldn't depend on being the most technical person in the family. Household protection means each family phone runs its own full VØID-SCRY — the same Moat, the same Heather, the same silence.

    • A full guardian per phone — not a watered-down family tier.

    • Nothing for your family to learn or manage — no chat, no pop-ups, no alerts to decode.

    Questions

    Asked, answered — plainly.

    Does VØID-SCRY send my data anywhere?

    No. There is no server, no cloud account, and no analytics pipeline. Heather lives entirely on the phone, the reports are generated on the phone, and by design there is no user tracking — the guardian couldn't report on you even if it wanted to. That isn't a policy promise; it's the architecture.

    Does Heather ever go online?

    Only to update herself. Once a day, over Wi-Fi, she fetches the latest threat list — the newest trackers and malicious domains to watch for. That's the whole trip: she takes in a list and sends nothing about you. There is no cloud, no account, and no conversation.

    Will Heather chat with me, or pop up notifications?

    No. Chat is retired as an interface, by design. Heather is silent: she guards, she watches, she heals, and once a week she files her proof report. Your phone stays your phone.

    What phones does it run on?

    Android today — proven on a basic Galaxy A17 with 4 GB of RAM, which is rather the point: the guardian was built light enough for ordinary phones, not just flagships. An iPhone version is scoped and ready, left as an option for a future buyer to build and fund.

    What happens if protection stops working?

    First, the guardian heals itself — it restarts and restores its own protection. And if you turn on the fail-closed option, a drop in protection is announced loudly, never silently. You will never be left believing you're guarded when you're not.

    How can I get it — or buy the whole thing?

    Users: join the waitlist above and you'll be first in line when seats open. Buyers and partners: write to blackpantherx83@gmail.com — details, the demo, and the app are available under a mutual NDA, and an independent security audit is quoted and ready to engage.
